capabilities: Preview static HTML files in a sandboxed iframe with scripts off by default
Edit text, link targets, and image properties by clicking page elements
Save edits as source-range patches that leave untouched markup unchanged
Back up draft snapshots and three-way-merge disk conflicts
Link notes to HTML files via [[page.html]] and show backlinks, outlinks, and referenced resources
extras: Desktop-only (requires Obsidian 1.7.2+); no mobile support. README warns uninstalling the plugin deletes drafts stored in its folder, and that page scripts are off by default and should only be enabled for trusted files. The listing carries an 'not reviewed by Obsidian staff' badge.
motivation: The README positions HTML pages as notes with freer layout and interaction than Markdown, since pages can use full CSS and optional scripts.
problem: Obsidian treats Markdown as the note format, so HTML files in the vault have no preview, no editing workflow, and no integration with links or embeddings.
summary: Visual editor that opens .html/.htm vault files in a sandboxed preview and edits text, links, and images through a sidebar workbench.
